_comment: The user-behaviour scenario for the JOSM example: seven steps a user repeats,
each with the parts of the screen that must change as a result.
Nothing here is a hard-coded pixel coordinate. The guest publishes
where its widgets and map objects actually are (see PATCH-LEDGER.md, patch 1),
and every point below is resolved from that at run time:
{"target": "building/13/5163"}   an object the application located for us
{"widget": "map", "at": [fx, fy]}  a fraction inside a named widget
Why this matters beyond tidiness: a coordinate written down from a screenshot
is only true for the window size, zoom level and layout it was read at, and
when it stops being true the driver still clicks — it just clicks the wrong
thing, which looks exactly like an application that did nothing. Resolving
names against the running application removes that whole failure mode, and the
run aborts if a name cannot be resolved rather than falling back to a guess.
The remaining fractions are sub-widget positions the guest does not report
individually (a cell inside the layer row, blank space inside the map). They
are relative to a real widget, so they survive a panel moving or resizing.
Deliberate: no menus, no dialogs, no window close (an uncontained guest
System.exit takes the shared JVM down with every tenant — #156).

layerEye is the one point the guest does not publish, so it is a fraction inside the layers panel and must be re-derived whenever the window size changes. Measured at 1920x1080 by capturing the NATIVE X display at 1:1 and cropping the panel at its own published bounds: the row's visibility eye (JOSM's LayerListDialog column 3) sits at (61.7, 32.2) of 325x208, hence 0.190, 0.155. Do not measure this through the browser -- deriving it from a screenshot needs the canvas origin, and an 11 px error there produced 0.104, which was confidently wrong. The native display has no such offset.

How the old value failed is worth knowing. At 0.19 the click landed at guest y=102 against a row centred on 95, i.e. on its bottom edge, and it collapsed the Layers panel instead of toggling the layer. Everything after that clicked the Tags title bar that had moved up into the space. The visible symptom was layer-hide PASSING and layer-show failing -- the hide only appeared to work because moving the pointer off the map drops JOSM's hover highlight, which repaints the map crop. A step can pass for a reason unrelated to what it tests.
_park: Where the pointer is parked before an at-rest reading is taken. JOSM
highlights whatever the pointer is over, so an at-rest snapshot taken with
the pointer on the map is not comparable with one taken after the last step
left it on a panel — the 'returned to start' check then reports drift that
is only a mouse position. Parking it at the same harmless place makes that
check mean what it says: leftover state.

cycle.why: selects one building way; both panels fill with its tags
selection moves to a different object, two rows and two columns away
clears the selection; verified 262 px clear of any object

three zoom steps in, each halving the scale. keystrokes rather than the wheel: a keystroke is a discrete, deterministic event. expectScale is asserted so a run that zooms by a different amount fails here instead of quietly reporting different memory later
three steps back out, returning to the starting scale exactly — which is what makes the steady profile self-checking
hides the data layer: a full-viewport repaint with no geometry
restores it, also byte-identical to the start
